subject: Lifeline Renewal — SLA add-on + credit + pricing request
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Lifeline renewal — initial ask for concession package

Team,

Quick context: ClearPath (Lifeline product) is up for renewal 11/15. They called today expressing strong price sensitivity after an internal budget reforecast and competitor pressure (they're running a pilot with a lower-cost vendor). Customer is strategic: heavy embeddings + low latency inference; current ARR ~ $420k. Renewal baseline is $435k for 12 months.

Customer asks (summary):
- 20% off list for first 12 months (applied as term discount)
- One-time $45k credit to cover migration/testing costs
- Reset to a 12-month term starting at renewal date (they were on 6 months)
- Add 99.9% SLA commitment + 3x credits for sustained downtime incidents (they need contractual comfort for latency-sensitive workloads)

Why escalated: AE tried standard concession routes; CS (Monica) says usage growth is contingent on these terms. The deal will likely churn if we don't move — they already have a competing PoC.

Attached: SOW_ClearPath_v3.pdf, pricing-model-clearpath.xlsx, usage-summary-Q3.csv.

Ask for this thread: executive / deal-desk signoff or guidance by COB 2026-10-05 so we can present a final counter to the customer. If full concessions are too aggressive, please propose an alternate combo (smaller discount + higher SLA credit cap).

Next steps I propose:
- Vivek: quick thumbs up / redline?
- Karthik: can Legal scope SLA add-on language and acceptable credit caps without a full PG review?
- Monica: confirm renewal health metrics (NPS, adoption signals) for pack rationale — attached usage summary as start.

Thanks — Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0128
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Lifeline renewal — initial ask for concession package

Aisha — thanks for the concise summary. A few initial thoughts:

- 20% + $45k credit + term reset + SLA add-on is a material concession for $420k ARR. We need commercial justification tied to realistic retention uplift (why will they not churn otherwise?).
- Alternative we should consider: 12% list discount + $25k credit + targeted SLA commitment limited to the Lifeline production cluster (not blanket org-level SLA) + performance-based earnback (if usage grows 25% in 6 months, concession steps back).

Karthik, can Legal draft a narrow SLA appendix that caps our maximum exposure (and limits credit triggers to verified infra outages)? Also confirm that a $45k credit is allowable under our concession matrix for this ARR band or if this requires VP/COO approval.

Monica, please send: churn risk indicators, contract value over last 12 months, and the competitor PoC details (timeline & scope).

If we take the alternative plan above, I can likely approve at VP level. If they insist on the full ask, escalate to COO for exceptional authority.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Liz Harper <liz@clearpath.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@clearpath.ai, finance@clearpath.ai
Date: 2026-10-06T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Lifeline renewal — initial ask for concession package

Aisha / Monica —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed alternatives. Background for clarity: finance needs a firm number by 10/12 to include in the Q4 budget. The competitor PoC is early but their pricing model is materially lower for the first year; we would need similar economics to justify staying. Our adoption is strong in the test groups, but moving to org-wide is contingent on predictable SLOs.

We prefer the full package you outlined, but understand you may push back — our ask is flexibility on both price and the SLA warranty. If you can reflect any compromise in writing, procurement and finance will prioritize the review.

Liz
Procurement Lead, ClearPath Analytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Lifeline renewal — legal review and conditional signoff

Vivek / Aisha — forwarding my notes after reviewing attachments and prior notes.

On Sun, Oct 4, 2026 at 13:30 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Aisha — thanks for the concise summary. A few initial thoughts:
> ...

My assessment and conditional approval:

- We can accept a 15% term discount for the first 12 months (applied as a contract amendment) and a $30k one-time credit tied to migration/testing milestones.
- SLA add-on: Legal will draft a scoped SLA appendix limited to the Lifeline production cluster and to incidents attributable to Redwood service failure. Credit triggers will be capped at 3x daily token value and an annual maximum equal to 10% of ARR.
- Term reset to 12 months is operationally fine; ensure billing aligns with start date.

Conditions:
1) Customer signs the SLA appendix and the amended SOW as-is (no unilateral extension of coverage).
2) We include a 6-month usage-based clawback: if trial usage drops below 60% of current production baseline at month 6, up to 50% of the $30k credit becomes payable back in credits against future invoices.
3) Any deviation above the approved set (higher credit or deeper discount) requires COO signoff.

Vivek, this is within standard VP approval thresholds if you confirm the final commercial structure (15% + $30k + limited SLA). If you approve, I will prepare the SLA appendix and route to DocuSign (draft link: https://na1.documents.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456).

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
